paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: Probing accuracy with reduced training data.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the probing accuracy of two multilingual BERT models—mBERT and XLM-R—as a function of training data size, ranging from 0 to 2000. The x-axis, labeled "Train size," is linearly scaled with tick marks at intervals of 250, from 0 to 2000. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," is also linearly scaled, ranging from 80 to 94 with tick marks every 2 units. The mBERT model is represented by a light blue dashed line with cross markers, starting at approximately 82.5 accuracy at a train size of 0 and gradually increasing to about 89.5 at a train size of 2000. The XLM-R model is shown with a dark blue solid line and cross markers, beginning at approximately 84.5 accuracy at train size 0 and rising more steeply to reach about 92.0 accuracy at train size 2000. Both lines show a general upward trend in accuracy with increasing training data, with XLM-R consistently outperforming mBERT across all train sizes.
